main_body: Flat desert sand ground patch (64x48 px) with sparse speckles, small dune-ridge marks and pebbles; no standing volume
top_band: none: terrain tile, uniform sand tone #dbb26b with occasional lighter/darker speckle rows; no standing top/front structure
evidence: Terrain ground tile, not a standing object. The column scan shows a uniform sand tone L=182 with 1-row speckle accents (L=204 and L=156) and no top/front structure. The 3/4 contract does not apply to flat ground, and no side faces or standing volume are drawn. It is a seamless repeating sand patch, so it passes as terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours and a median of 4 colours per tile, against 26 per tile and 80 colours for the grass reference. The paving reference has 7, so it is also below that. The sand has a base tone, one lighter and one darker speckle, plus a small number of extra accents, so about 3 real steps against 5-6 for Beodeul. Speckles are sparse and the pattern repeats exactly every 16 px (visible tiling of the same dune marks at x=16 intervals), which looks mechanical. There is no flat-fill block of 5x5 and no outline to judge (terrain), but the shading is shallow and the tile information is far below the grass reference. Fails on shading depth and density.
